title: Man. Post. Cap. IX: PLAC tip — satisfaction imputed after faith, not before existence; tip before 'alius pro nobis'
pass_a_gloss: Placeus: the cases are not alike. Satisfaction is imputed to believers after faith, never before existence. 'Satisfied in Christ' is not a Scripture phrase to be taken properly; it means only Christ satisfied for us. Tip before he presses 'another sinned for us' and the rest.
pass_b_english: PLAC. This example is not like, nor does it in any way overturn my reasoning. Christ's satisfaction is indeed imputed to us believing, but that imputation follows our faith, does not precede it, still less so as to precede our existence. For we are justified by faith, not before faith. When therefore we are said to have satisfied in Christ, as the phrase does not stand in Scripture, so it ought to be taken conveniently, and cannot be understood properly. The sense ought to be no other than this, Christ satisfied for us.
source_text: PLAC. Hoc exemplum non est simile, nec meam ratiocinationem ullo modo evertit. Imputatur quidem nobis credentibus Christi satisfactio, sed ea imputatio fidem nostram sequitur, non antecedit, nedum ut antecedat nostram existentiam. Iustificamur enim fide, non ante fidem. Cum igitur dicimur satisfecisse in Christo, ut locutio non extat in Scriptura, sic commode accipi debet, nec proprie intelligi potest. Sensus alius esse non debet quam iste, Christus satisfecit pro nobis.

choices.choice: Satisfaction imputation follows faith; tip before 'alius pro nobis' / further
